title: Directional Channel Representation and Effective Rank Bounds in Industrial MIMO Channels
content: Metal equipment in industrial buildings creates many propagation paths, but paths with similar array responses can concentrate power in the same multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) modes. This study examines how path directions, path powers, and array geometry jointly determine the modal power spectrum. We develop a directional cell representation that groups ray-traced paths by delay and by three-dimensional departure and arrival directions while retaining their coherent complex gains. We derive a reconstruction error bound that relates direction errors to array aperture. We also relate mechanism-specific angular power to statistical spatial correlation. For individual channel matrices, a weighted participation-ratio identity accounts for element power imbalance and correlation energy. A correction based on the second and third modal power moments tightens the lower bound on entropy-based effective rank. These relations guide a two-parameter spectrum predictor. In three controlled industrial layouts, the cell representation preserves the main modal structure at held-out 28 GHz positions and in 140 GHz cross-frequency tests. From an open aisle to a metal corridor, the azimuth-based effective cell count rises substantially, while the entropy-based effective rank rises only slightly. The predictor reduces the mean Jensen–Shannon divergence by 28.5% relative to a mean-spectrum baseline at held-out 28 GHz receiver positions.
